name: Fifty-One Threshold Poems (physical only)
creator: Adaeze Volkov
description: A hand-letterpress poetry collection that exists exclusively in a physical edition of 300 numbered copies, never licensed for neural-feed or digital distribution — a deliberate refusal Volkov has called 'the only honest form for this work.' The poems explore the phenomenology of augmentation thresholds: the moment before a BCI is first activated, the instant of waking after geneware takes hold, the particular silence of a chrome limb not yet learned. The language is spare and precise, drawing on Igbo praise-poetry structure and imagist compression.
medium: physical letterpress (300 copies only, no digital edition)
cultural_impact: The collection's refusal of neural-feed distribution made it an immediate artifact of countercultural significance — owning a copy is a statement, and the poems circulate in handwritten transcription among communities who can't afford the physical object. Widely considered the defining poetry collection of the early augmentation era.
controversy: Volkov has legally pursued two pirate neural-feed uploads of the poems, winning one injunction and losing one. Some critics argue the physical-only stance is classist, limiting the work to those with money and connections. Volkov counters that handwritten transcription — the way the poems actually circulate on the Shelf — is the form of transmission the work was always meant to have.
story_hooks: Copy #7 of the 300 was gifted to a Shelf community library and subsequently stolen; its current location is unknown and its recovery has become a minor obsession in certain circles.

A neural-feed pirate has uploaded all 51 poems with an anonymous introduction arguing that Volkov's physical-only stance is itself a form of corporate compliance — keeping radical language away from those who need it most.
Volkov is dying and has left instructions for the destruction of her personal copy and all correspondence about the poems — someone close to her is trying to decide whether to comply.
